extractions.value: Clinical features of stiffness and spasms; abolition of muscular hyperactivity under general anesthesia; EMG showing continuous motor unit potentials at rest; response to diazepam and baclofen; exclusion of neuromyotonia and tetanus
extractions.quote: In our opinion, the abolition of muscular hyperactivity under general anesthesia confirmed the diagnosis of SPS in this case, and certainly ruled out the possibility of neuromyotonia... the lack of history of a wound or trauma, the duration and persistence of symptoms after being treated with antitetanus immune globulin, and the lack of other common signs of tetanus such as trismus and risus sardonicus suggested that the diagnosis of SPS was more likely than that of ''chronic'' tetanus.

SPS, first described in 1956 by Moersch and Woltman, is characterized by persistent, painful axial and proximal limb muscle rigidity and spasms exacerbated by sensory or motor stimuli and abolished by sleep or general anesthesia.

extractions.value: First documented case of SPS associated with histologically proven thymoma. Patient had atypical features for SPS including clinical myokymia, brisk reflexes, equivocal plantar responses, and hyperhidrosis. Muscular hyperactivity was abolished under general anesthesia, confirming SPS and ruling out neuromyotonia. Patient developed ocular myasthenia gravis after thymectomy, which resolved spontaneously within 12 months. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies remained undetectable throughout.
extractions.quote: We report the first documented case of SPS associated with histologically proven thymoma... Our patient also had some atypical features for SPS, such as clinical myokymia, brisk reflexes, equivocal plantar responses, and hyperhydrosis... the patient later developed ocular myasthenia, which later resolved spontaneously... Acetylcholine receptor antibodies remain undetectable.
